data.standardized_narrative: At the 2019 year end Syndicate 6103 reported opening gross claims outstanding of GBP 11.009m (prior year). Gross prior-year development was a small adverse movement of c.GBP 0.63m (about 5.7% of opening claims), i.e. a modest strengthening of reserves. The report notes a net deterioration of GBP 0.3m and attributes uncertainty to material exposure from 2018 catastrophe events (notably Hurricanes Florence and Michael and California wildfires). Reinsurance recoveries partially offset gross deterioration resulting in a smaller net impact.
raw_causal_phrases: The movement in the net provisions for claims includes a deterioration of GBP 0.3m (2018: deterioration of GBP 0.1m).
In 2019, there has been an overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 0.4m (2018: deficit of GBP 0.1m) due primarily to a decrease in claims estimates.
The syndicate has material exposure to the hurricanes Florence and Michael and California Wildfires in the 2018 year of account. This increases the uncertainty of the syndicate's total reserves.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (gross) was derived from the published gross claims development triangle (gross column for 2017). The notes explicitly state only the NET prior-year deterioration (GBP 0.3m); no explicit gross 'movement in prior years' line was provided. Calculation excludes 2018 and 2019 columns per methodology. RITC commutations into Syndicate 2791 are present (small amounts) and could modestly affect comparability; overall confidence is medium-high.
